memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Put it under the ledge of the altar so that it is halfway up the altar. Make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze. The poles are to be inserted into the rings so they will be on two sides of the altar when it is carried. Make the altar hollow, out of boards. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain." - Exodus 27:5-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Like the ark and the table, the altar was fitted with rings and poles so it could be carried. And it was made hollow — built of boards rather than solid metal, light enough to be lifted and moved. Wherever Israel travelled, the place of sacrifice travelled with them.

This is a quiet mercy. God did not fix the altar to one location and tell His people to return there when they needed forgiveness. It went where they went. Whatever unfamiliar wilderness they camped in, the means of approaching God was right there in the middle of the camp. Access was never far away.

The same is gloriously true for us, and more so. We do not journey to a place to find forgiveness; we come to a Person, and He is always near. There is no location where Christ's sacrifice is unavailable to you — no country, no season, no depth of failure that puts you out of range. Hebrews says He is able to save completely those who come to God through Him, because He always lives to intercede for them (Heb 7:25). Wherever you are today, the altar has travelled with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I ever feel too far away — geographically or spiritually — to come to God?
How does it comfort me that access to God travels with me everywhere?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that forgiveness is never out of reach. Wherever I go and whatever I face, the way to You through Christ is always open. Draw me near today. Amen.
